title: Untyped knowledge-layer writes cause authorship erosion, confidence laundering, and reflexive contamination
content:
## Claim

Provenance over ephemeral artifacts is not enough when skills write into persistent memory the human treats as their own thinking.

Three contaminations follow:

1. **Authorship erosion** — cannot tell human notes from skill drafts months later
2. **Confidence laundering** — low-confidence agent claims land as flat facts and get cited as prior
3. **Reflexive contamination** — later skills read agent-authored vault text as if it were human prior thinking

## Remedy direction

Force typed epistemic standing at write time (author, producer skill, epistemic mode, confidence, sources, review status) so the vault stays queryable along *mine vs agent* axes.

## Methodology grounding
The claims below live in the plugin's `data/methodology/` corpus; the relationship is stated per claim.

- **[[agents are simultaneously methodology executors and subjects creating a unique trust asymmetry]]** — BUILDS_ON. The asymmetry is why these three failures are structural rather than careless: the agent writing the record is also the subject the record will later be judged by, so nothing inside the agent's own reasoning distinguishes its inference from its evidence. Typing the write moves that distinction outside the agent.
- **[[agent self-memory should be architecturally separate from user knowledge systems]]** — RELATES_TO. Reflexive contamination is precisely what an unseparated self-space produces: the agent's working beliefs leak into the corpus it is supposed to be reporting on.
description: When skills write flat statements into long-lived memory, humans lose authorship boundaries and agents later treat agent text as human prior.
